colorgrade_enabled.comment: Master toggle. When off the grading pass is a no-op and the image is vanilla.

adaptive_enabled.comment: Brightens dark places and settles back in the light, like an eye adjusting.

grade_adaptive.comment: Let the world grade itself: time of day, weather, biome, indoors, depth, underwater. Off leaves your own settings reaching the screen unmodified.

pbr_entitylighting.comment: Give creatures the same microfacet lighting as the terrain they stand on: sun specular, sky term, torch highlights and a wet response. Off leaves them with vanilla's flat diffuse.

pbr_particlelighting.comment: Give falling leaves, pollen, dust, sparks and smoke the same lighting as everything else. They belonged to no lighting model at all before.

weather_cloudsfromgame.comment: Read cloud positions from the game's own cloud renderer so shadows land under the clouds that cast them. Off falls back to a noise field that moves and covers correctly but cannot line up with the sky.

pbr_enabled.comment: Derived normal maps give stone, wood and gravel real surface relief. Off by default: this is the only setting that patches the shader drawing the world.

weather_enabled.comment: Rain makes exposed surfaces wet: smoother, more reflective and darker, drying out after the rain stops.

colorgrade_exposure.comment: Linear exposure multiplier applied before the tonemap. 1.0 is unchanged.

colorgrade_contrast.comment: Pivots around display mid-grey. 1.0 is unchanged, 0 is flat.

colorgrade_saturation.comment: 0 is greyscale, 1.0 is unchanged, above 1 oversaturates.

colorgrade_temperature.comment: White balance. Negative is cooler/bluer, positive is warmer/oranger.

colorgrade_tonemapstrength.comment: Blend between vanilla output and the filmic ACES curve. 0 disables the tonemap only.

adaptive_darkgain.comment: Exposure multiplier in pitch darkness. 1.0 disables the brightening.

adaptive_brightgain.comment: Exposure multiplier in full light. 1.0 leaves bright scenes as authored.

adaptive_brightenseconds.ingui: Eye adaptation: time to adapt to dark
adaptive_brightenseconds.comment: Seconds to settle after entering darkness. Slow, like real dark adaptation.

adaptive_darkenseconds.ingui: Eye adaptation: time to adapt to light
adaptive_darkenseconds.comment: Seconds to settle after stepping into light. Fast, like real light adaptation.

pbr_normalstrength.comment: Global multiplier on the relief. 1.0 is the tuned look, 0 is flat.

pbr_specularstrength.comment: Microfacet specular, and the energy it removes from the diffuse. 1.0 is the tuned look, 0 is exactly vanilla.

pbr_roughnessbias.comment: Shifts every material's roughness. Negative is glossier and wetter, positive is drier and more matte.

pbr_metalresponse.comment: How metallic reflective materials read. 0 gives every surface a white highlight; 1 lets metals tint theirs by their own colour.

pbr_ambientspecular.comment: Strength of the ambient sky highlight. Without it metal in shade or indoors has no highlight at all.

pbr_specularaa.comment: Widens highlights by how much the normal varies within a pixel, which is what stops rough surfaces sparkling as you move. Leave at 1 unless comparing.

pbr_detaildistance.comment: Distance at which surface relief has faded out. Higher shows more detail at range and more aliasing with it.

pbr_blocklight.comment: Strength of highlights from torches, lava, lanterns and glowing blocks. Works underground and at night, where the sun cannot reach.

pbr_blocklightdir.comment: 0 treats block light as coming from everywhere. 1 estimates where the light actually is, so highlights track a torch as you pass it.

weather_wetness.comment: How wet rain makes surfaces look. Above 1 exaggerates past anything physical.

weather_dryingseconds.comment: How long a soaked surface takes to dry once the rain stops. Surfaces wet in seconds either way; the slow dry is what makes it read as weather.

weather_raincover.comment: How exposed to the sky a surface must be before rain reaches it. Raise it to keep porches, canopy and doorways dry.

weather_fogstrength.comment: How much rain thickens the air. 0 leaves vanilla fog alone.

weather_fogtint.comment: How much rain drains colour from the fog and cools it. Shifts vanilla's fog colour rather than replacing it.

weather_cloudshadow.comment: Depth of cloud shadows on the ground at noon. Cover and drift direction come from the game's own cloud density and wind, so shadows thicken and travel with the real sky.

weather_cloudscale.comment: Blocks across one cloud cell. Larger means broader, slower-moving shadows.

weather_clouddrift.comment: How fast cloud shadows travel, in cells per minute, along the world's wind direction.

weather_frost.comment: How much frost changes a surface, on top of the game's own frost. Vanilla decides where frost is and tints it white; this makes it behave like frost - rough, with the highlight of whatever it covers killed.

weather_snowdusting.comment: A thin film of snow on surfaces the sky can see. Does not compete with the game's own snow blocks - this is the dusting on fence rails, crates and rocks.

weather_ripples.comment: How hard rain lands in the water it left. Rides the material shader's normal, so it needs PseudoPBR on and a wet, up-facing, sky-exposed surface.

weather_overcast.comment: How completely cloud cover diffuses the sun. Weakens direct highlights and lifts the sky term, rather than darkening everything.

weather_cloudheight.comment: World height the shadow-casting cloud deck sits at. Decides how far a shadow slides from what casts it as the sun drops.

grade_stylestrength.comment: How far toward the chosen style to lean. The style is one more capped contributor on top of the world, not a preset that replaces your settings. Set Style in the config file: None, Filmic, Muted, Vivid, Cold or Warm.

grade_timeofday.comment: Golden hour warmth near sunrise and sunset, and the desaturated blue shift of night vision.

grade_weather.comment: How much rain and cloud cover drain colour and contrast out of the scene.

grade_biome.comment: Heat, cold, aridity and lushness at the player's position. Deserts warm and glare, tundra drains, rainforest saturates.

grade_indoor.comment: Firelight warmth and harder shadows once the sky can no longer see you.

grade_depth.comment: Colour draining out with depth below sea level.

grade_underwater.comment: The blue-green shift of being submerged. Water absorbs red first and blue last.

grade_response.comment: How long the grade takes to travel most of the way to a new one. Too fast and a doorway is a flash.

pbr_emissive.comment: How much emitting surfaces read as hot rather than merely bright. Driven by the game's own glow data, so a forge lights a room and a white marble block does not.

pbr_emissivetemperature.comment: How much a bright emitter shifts toward white at its core, the way real hot things do. Most of what makes something read as hot rather than as painted orange.

pbr_emissiveflicker.comment: How much a flame is allowed to breathe. Seeded by position, so two torches on one wall do not flicker in step.

pbr_emissivebloom.comment: How much emitters add to the game's own bloom pass. Driven by actual emission rather than pixel brightness, which is the difference between a bloom that finds light sources and one that finds snow.

pbr_foliage.comment: Sunlight scattering through foliage, so a canopy with the sun behind it glows. Applies to whatever vanilla treats as wind-affected: leaves, grass, crops, flowers.

pbr_cavity.comment: Occlusion in the grooves, from the material normal's curvature. The scale vanilla's SSAO cannot see - mortar lines, plank gaps, bark furrows. Costs four extra texture samples.

pbr_dapple.comment: Sunlight broken into moving patches by the leaves overhead. Only appears where the game's own sun light level says there is a canopy above - open ground and interiors are untouched. Gaps brighten by as much as the shade between them darkens, so it never dims the scene overall. 0 is vanilla.

pbr_particlespecular.comment: How much of the particle specular lobe reaches the image. Low on purpose: a highlight that reads as detail on a wall reads as twinkling noise on a cloud of dust.

pbr_entityroughness.comment: How matte creatures read. They have no derived material atlas, so one roughness covers all of them.

pbr_entityspecular.comment: How much of the creature specular lobe reaches the image. 0 is vanilla.

pbr_entitydebug.comment: Numbered in the entity path's own terms, not the material system's: 0 off, 1 the specular lobe alone, 2 wetness, 3 how much the scene is holding the mod back.

pbr_debugview.comment: 0 normal rendering. 1 normal map, 2 roughness, 3 specular mask, 4 relief only, 5 highlight only, 6 world-space normal, 7 reflectance, 8 roughness as shaded, 9 block-light direction, 10 wetness, 11 rain ripples, 12 crevice occlusion, 13 foliage transmission, 14 emission.

weather_clouddebugview.comment: 0 off. 1 shows the cloud shadow field on its own at full strength, with vanilla's shadow map out of the way. 2 is the calibration view: the game's cloud tiles drawn straight down with no offset toward the sun - stand still, look up, look down, and the pattern on the ground should match the clouds in the sky. 3 shows the sampling window's own tile grid and its edge.
